proposal_reality_cards.headline: The House passed utility-accountability bills four times (105-1, 101-0, 118-0, 114-0); every one died in Senate Judiciary. What became law is oversight machinery: Santee Cooper reform (Act 90 of 2021), restarted PSC elections (Acts 74/75 of 2025), public-witness rights (Act 41 of 2025).
proposal_reality_cards.legislator_utility_ties: H4260 (2019) banned utility gifts/campaign contributions to the legislators' panel that screens utility regulators — the closest match to the citizens' financial-ties concern. No bill adds a utility-specific disclosure duty for legislators; annual Statements of Economic Interests exist under the ethics law (Title 8) but are not utility-specific.
proposal_reality_cards.venue: Rates are set case-by-case by the PSC; the legislature controls who sits on it, its procedures, and utility conduct rules.
open_questions: Why Senate Judiciary never took up the House-passed bills (no committee record exists)
Whether the 2025 changes answer the concern or leave the money-ties piece open
What SEI forms do and don't show about utility ties

proposal_reality_cards.headline: Officially studied once — Act 187 of 2020 created the Electricity Market Reform Measures Study Committee (House 81-31, Senate 41-0). Every actual market-opening bill (H5439, H5440, S878, H5525) was filed in 2026 and died in first committee without a vote.
proposal_reality_cards.venue: Service territories and retail regulation are state statute (a General Assembly lever); wholesale markets and transmission are federal (FERC).
open_questions: What the 2020 study committee's report concluded (outside this bill record)
The citizens' flagged tradeoff: can the grid support competition?
Whether the 2026 filings are momentum or a one-session reaction to rate debates

proposal_reality_cards.headline: Already policy — via the budget, not a bill. After S16 passed both chambers and died in conference (2022), FY 2022-23 proviso 1.101 ordered the half-credit personal finance graduation requirement into regulation; Regulation Document 5130 took effect May 26, 2023 (first bound class graduates 2027). Statute 59-29-410 has required financial-literacy instruction since 2005.
proposal_reality_cards.venue: Graduation requirement: State Board of Education regulation. Statute and funding: General Assembly. Nothing in the record addresses adult financial education.
open_questions: Is the proposal satisfied by the 2023 requirement (no outcome data until 2027)?
Did the citizens' intent include adults (untouched by any bill)?
The citizens' flagged tradeoff: education does not lower prices

proposal_reality_cards.headline: 80 bills, the narrowest wins. Full elimination (H3378) and ~24 homestead-increase bills died in House Ways and Means without votes — except S768 (Senate 44-0, then died there). Vehicle-tax bills: 13 filed, zero votes, none statewide. Enacted instead: targeted fixes, the S866 municipal sales-tax swap (Act 228 of 2026), and one-year budget relief (proviso 117.220's extra $25,000 homestead exemption; 117.208/117.191 income-tax acceleration).
proposal_reality_cards.venue: Property tax is local revenue under state rules; schools/local government depend on it (the citizens' flagged tradeoff). Act 388 of 2006 already exempts owner-occupied homes from school operating taxes (Homestead Exemption Fund, 11-11-156).
open_questions: Price tag of each design (no fiscal notes in this record)
How replacement revenue works — does the S866 swap model scale?
Why House Ways and Means has not taken up even Senate-passed S768

deliberation_prompts: Four utility-accountability bills passed the House 438-1 combined and died in Senate Judiciary without a hearing record. What would have to change for the fifth to be different?
The 2020 market-reform study committee was created by law. What did it conclude, and does it answer the feasibility worry from the Community Conversations?
Retail-choice bills appeared for the first time in 2026, right after two years of rate debates. Momentum, or a one-session reaction?
The personal-finance graduation requirement is in force; the first bound class graduates in 2027. What would 'done' versus 'needs more' look like?

Homestead increases die in House Ways and Means even after a 44-0 Senate vote — yet the same chamber wrote a one-year $25,000 exemption into the budget. Is the objection to the policy, or to making it permanent?
H3378 promises dollar-for-dollar reimbursement for eliminating property taxes. What replaces local revenue, and does the S866 swap model scale?
No bill in eight years proposes ending the vehicle property tax statewide. Untried, or off the table because county budgets depend on it?
Big energy packages pass; consumer billing protections never get a vote. Wrong committee, or riding alone when they need a package?
Which parts of the transparency concern are about the PSC's process, and which are about legislators themselves (ethics law)?
